name: Cerebellar Malformation

criteria.description: Neuroimaging evidence of cerebellar structural abnormalities (hypoplasia, agenesis, or dysplasia) on MRI
Presence of cerebellar dysfunction signs such as ataxia, dysmetria, or hypotonia
Exclusion of acquired causes of cerebellar damage (e.g., infection, trauma, neoplasm)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with cerebellar development (optional supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Neuroimaging confirmation of cerebellar malformation plus clinical signs of cerebellar dysfunction, with exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Gait and limb ataxia due to cerebellar dysfunction
Decreased muscle tone commonly observed in infancy
Impaired ability to control movement distance and speed

common.notes: Involuntary eye movements associated with cerebellar dysfunction
Slurred or slow speech due to impaired coordination

occasional.notes: Mild to moderate intellectual disability in some cases
Generalized weakness secondary to cerebellar involvement

rare.notes: Occasionally associated with posterior fossa malformations
Rare respiratory insufficiency due to brainstem involvement
Poor suck and swallow reflexes in infancy

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; metabolic screening to exclude acquired causes
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar hypoplasia, agenesis, or dysplasia
Possible associated brainstem or supratentorial abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as RELN, VLDLR, or others involved in cerebellar development
other: Developmental assessment revealing motor coordination deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle
Partial or complete agenesis of the cerebellar vermis

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties with failure to thrive
references: Parisi MA. Cerebellar malformations: clinical and molecular features. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2009.
Barkovich AJ, et al. Classification system for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012.
